# Rewrite a document

Use this procedure when a request names a file to rewrite.

1. Read the file that the request names.
2. If the file is a skill (`SKILL.md`), a subagent definition or a slash-command file, stop. A rewrite of it is a skill edit, so hand off to the writing-skills skill. If that skill is not available, say why you did not rewrite the file.
3. Choose the target.
   - Rewrite the file in place when it is not a symbolic link, git tracks it and it has no uncommitted edits. Run all three commands. The first two must succeed, and the third must print nothing.

     ```bash
     test ! -L <path>
     git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>
     git status --porcelain -- <path>
     ```

   - In every other case, outside a git repository too, write `<stem>.ste<ext>` beside the file: `setup.ste.md` beside `setup.md`. If that file exists, stop and ask.
4. Run the linter on the original, and keep its counts:

   ```bash
   python3 <this-skill-dir>/scripts/ste-lint.py --json <path>
   ```

5. Rewrite the file section by section, under the meaning rules in SKILL.md. Keep these parts unchanged: the frontmatter, fenced and inline code, URLs and link targets, quoted text and the table structure. Keep the headings too, unless the request asks to change them. The prose inside a table cell may change.
6. Run the linter on the result.
7. Reply with a short summary: the path that you wrote, the audience and rule set, the linter counts before and after, and any `Kept as-is:` notes. Never commit. In place, `git diff` shows the change and `git restore <path>` undoes it.
----
docs/guide.md
----
     1	---
     2	title: Label printer setup
     3	owner: facilities
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Label printer setup
     7	
     8	The label printer that is located in room 2.14 has been configured so that it can be utilized by everyone on the floor; however, it should be noted that the driver needs to be installed prior to the first print job being sent.
     9	
    10	## Install the driver
    11	
    12	In order to install the driver, the following command should be run from a terminal window:
    13	
    14	```bash
    15	sudo ./install-driver.sh --model LP-200 --queue floor2
    16	```
    17	
    18	If the installer reports "E_QUEUE: queue busy", it is recommended that you wait for a minute or so and then try again.
    19	
    20	## Paper sizes
    21	
    22	| Size | Use it for |
    23	|---|---|
    24	| 62 mm | address labels that are going to be sent out by post |
    25	| 29 mm | small labels that are used for the shelves |
    26	
    27	> Do not load third-party rolls. The warranty is void if you do.
    28	
    29	See the [vendor manual](https://example.com/lp-200/manual.pdf) for more information about the various options that are available.

---
title: Label printer setup
owner: facilities
---

# Label printer setup

Everyone on the floor can use the label printer in room 2.14. You need to install the driver before you send your first print job.

## Install the driver

To install the driver, you should run this command in a terminal window:

```bash
sudo ./install-driver.sh --model LP-200 --queue floor2
```

If the installer reports "E_QUEUE: queue busy", the recommended action is to wait about a minute and then try again.

## Paper sizes

| Size | Use it for |
|---|---|
| 62 mm | address labels that you send by post |
| 29 mm | small labels for the shelves |

> Do not load third-party rolls. The warranty is void if you do.

See the [vendor manual](https://example.com/lp-200/manual.pdf) for more information about the available options.
EOF
